findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The facility could benefit from a detail cleaning. There is observed soil accumulation around certain floors and walls throughout the facility. Also, accumulation was observed beneath and around large pieces of equipment. Ensure that detail cleaning occurs as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
A storage rack that stores freshly baked bread appeared to not have a covering on the top. Discussed with PIC and a baking sheet was placed on the top of the rack. Ensure that a baking sheet or any type of covering is placed over the rack whenever bread is being stored to protect against contamination.   

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The facility is in need of a deep cleaning. The floors, walls, and ceilings of both the back and the front of the house are accumulated with food/liquid splatter, dust, and overall debris. Ensure that all physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil accumulation. When cleaning, be sure to pull equipment that has wheels from the wall to throughly clean floors and walls.  


6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The facility would benefit from a detail cleaning. There is observed soil accumulation around most of the wall-to-floor corners of the facility, around doors and legs of equipment, under wheels, and under equipment. Mainly observed is food splash and bread crumbs. See that detail cleaning occurs as needed to prevent accumulation of soil. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed caulking on the hand sink next to the 3 part sink to be coming off of the hand sink and wall. Ensure caulking is replaced so the hand sink is sealed properly to the wall. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed the soda nozzles to be soiled. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Soda nozzles were pulled for cleaning. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Observed a spatula to be stored under a bread press, which is not a sanitized surface. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Spatula moved for cleaning. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16

Mop was observed to be in mop bucket and not in a position that allows air-dry. Ensure mops are hung in a way that allows to properly air-dry. Mop was COS.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

Observed employee food within the fridge that was unlabeled and stored with facility food.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Hand sink in kitchen contained several soiled food containers.

750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

Corrected Immediately

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
REPEAT> Observed the prepackaged brownies to not have ingredient and allergen labeling. Cookies now have this information, but it is needed for the brownies as well.
750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name; name, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed the bread on the racks to not be covered. Cover bread to prohibit the potential for contamination. Bread on stand up rack was placed in food grade bags and in use bread racks were covered with deli paper.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener blade to have an accumulation of debris on the blade. Scrub, wash, rinse and sanitize this.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
No soap was available in the women's restroom. Soap was provided during the inspection.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed brownies, cookies and bread baked and pre-packaged on the front counter to not have any labeling available. All products pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must have the common name of the product (which is posted today), the net contents of the package, a list of ingredients in order of predominance by weight and a list of artificial colors or flavors, and allergens.
750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name; name, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed two employees wash hands and use bare hands to turn off the faucet before getting paper towels to dry their hands. Hands should be washed for a full 20 seconds and then dried with a paper towel and then use the paper towel to turn off the faucet handle so as to not re-contaminate hands. Staff was educated on hand washing during inspection.
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink in the front to not be sealed to the wall. Since the last inspection, plywood panels covered with brick overlay have been added to the wall and cut around to fit the sink. Caulk the gaps that are present between the hand sink and this plywood overlay.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed duct tape on the corner of the prep table in the back room. Remove duct tape as it is not smooth and easily cleanable.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the inside of the top oven has bread sticking to the fan in the back and one of the wire racks. 2) the doors and handles of the reach in coolers in the back room, 3) the sandwich press with an accumulation of char, 4) the sandwich oven with an accumulation of char. Clean these non food contact surfaces. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor to be soiled in the following areas: 1) near the water heater in the small closet with soil and possible old mouse droppings, 2) underneath the coolers in the back room with debris and soil. Clean the floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed cooked pork in the reach in freezer to not be labeled with a date as to when it was opened. Manager was consulted during inspection and item was date marked as to the date it was opened.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed bread on the front counter to be uncovered. Bread was placed into bags during inspection. It was discussed that as long as bread it either on the shelves that have a cover on the top shelf or on the wheeled rack that has a cover on the top rack, it would not need to be covered. If on the table, bread should be protected from potential contamination.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed the top lip of a container to be chipped. Replace container. 2) Observed a drain pipe sticking out of the floor where a mop sink may have been in the corner near the water heater room to be covered with duct tape. Remove duct tape and provide an appropriate cover.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed sanitizer concentration in both the three compartment sink and sanitizer bucket to be 0 ppm chlorine. Both sanitizers were remade to 50 and 100 ppm chlorine respectively.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wet wiping cloth on the table near the kettles. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between uses.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the can opener blade to be soiled with food debris. Wash, rinse and sanitize can opener. 2) Observed the sandwich press to have an accumulation of char. Scrape, wash, rinse and sanitize press. 3) Inside bottom of sandwich oven has an accumulation of char. Clean the sandwich oven.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Observed the caulk at the three compartment sink to have gaps. Re-seal the three compartment sink to the wall.
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents. Provide properly constructed walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed tuna salad and cut tomatoes above 41 degrees in the top prep cooler. Cooler was turned down to allow food to maintain temperatures at or under 41 degrees. Tomatoes and tuna salad will be used in 4 hours or discarded. Facility also added ice and called the refrigeration repair company to service cooler.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the racks that hold the clean dishes to be soiled. Clean the racks that hold the clean dishes so no accumulated soil is visible. CORRECTED> Observed the bottom of the proofer to be soiled with dried dough and caked on flour. Proofer was cleaned during inspection.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed straws and lids being stored on the floor in the adjacent room. Store Single use items at least 6 inches off floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed loaves of bread stored directly adjacent to the handsink and to be able to be splashed during the handwashing process. During the inspection the manager and I both moved the baking sheet of loaves to the center of the shelving rack and they were moved against the handsink during maneuvering of routine business. Discussed placing a sheet of plexiglass or metal between the bread racks and the handsink to protect bread from handwashing splash. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 The single service knives are improperly being stored within a gold cup by the cash register. The knives are being stored handle in and handle out. Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Store knives so that the handle is presented out and available to be grabbed.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment: 750-1120 The frontline handsink has no available hot water. Manager Lois stated that the water was shut off due to a leak. The handsink has not been operable for several days and the sink in the back room is being used for handwashing. Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: 750-1120e The frontline handsink (not currently in use) and the backline sink faucet are soiled. Handsinks shall be maintained clean. Keep the handsink routinely cleaned and sanitized to allow for proper hand washing.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 The floor of the frontline around the legs and wheels of equipment is black with soil. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 The relatively new wood paneling installed by the silver coolers in the backroom is missing coving. You may use caulking as coving. Gap between the wood panel and the floor must be sealed. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 (REPEAT) Wood paneling installed around the backroom walls is not properly sealed. The surface facing into the kitchen must be properly sealed. (REPEAT) The wall directly behind the frontline ovens/soda fridge is damaged and drywall is damaged along area where the table hits the wall.  All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250  A container a horseradish spread was kept at room temperature above the sandwich prep. table. The container was marked 'Keep Refrigerated'. During the inspection, the spread was discarded. You may use time, temperature, or manufacturer's exemption as a control. If you choose, keep a container of the sauce at room temperature for up to four hours - time when spread is placed at room temp. must be clearly marked. Spread may also be kept in prep. cooler with other spreads so it is always held at 41F or below. Or, have available a note from the manufacturer that states the product is NOT potentially hazardous and is allowed to be stored at room temperature once opened without refrigeration for up to X amount of days/weeks/etc. All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 There is a small piece of wood being held with clamps below the cash machine. This piece of wood is not properly sealed. Paint/seal the bare wood surface.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
